svg.title: Moles & reacting masses
svg.desc: Mᵣ & composition: Ca(OH)₂: 40 + 2 × (16 + 1) = 74. Brackets multiply every atom inside. Oxygen percentage = 32/74 × 100 = 43.2%. Mᵣ has no unit; molar mass is 74 g/mol. Moles & particles: n = mass / molar mass. 11 g CO₂ / 44 g/mol = 0.25 mol. Particles = n × 6.02 × 10²³. This is 1.505 × 10²³ CO₂ molecules; each has three atoms. State whether counting atoms, molecules, ions or electrons. Reacting masses: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. 6.0 g Mg / 24 = 0.25 mol Mg. Mg : MgO = 2 : 2 → 0.25 mol MgO. Mass = 0.25 × 40 = 10 g MgO, oxygen in excess. Coefficients are mole ratios, not mass ratios. Find equation coefficients: Divide each mass by its molar mass; divide all moles by smallest; multiply to whole numbers. 2.4 g Mg, 1.6 g O₂, 4.0 g MgO → 0.10 : 0.05 : 0.10 mol → 2 : 1 : 2. Check atoms and total mass on both sides. Limiting vs excess: 0.30 mol Mg + 0.10 mol O₂: oxygen needs only 0.20 mol Mg. O₂ is limiting. MgO formed = 0.20 mol; Mg left = 0.10 mol. Use limiting amount for theoretical yield; extra excess reactant cannot increase it. Mass & uncertainty: An open vessel gains mass if oxygen enters; loses mass if gas escapes. Count all substances to conserve mass. Readings 24.2, 24.4, 24.6 → mean 24.4; range 0.4; half-range uncertainty ±0.2. Percentage uncertainty = 0.2/24.4 × 100 = 0.82%.
